bib.title: Generate rather than Retrieve: Large Language Models are Strong Context Generators

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Generate rather than Retrieve: Large Language Models are Strong Context Generators", Wenhao Yu, Dan Iter, Shuohang Wang, Yichong Xu, Mingxuan Ju, Soumya Sanyal, Chenguang Zhu, Michael Zeng, Meng Jiang (Notre Dame / Microsoft Cognitive Service Research / USC). The PDF says "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023". This copy is arXiv 2209.10063v3, dated 25 Jan 2023.
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/yu-2022-generate-rather-than-retrieve.pdf

COVERAGE: I read all 100,047 of 100,047 chars across 27 pages: the main text, the limitations and ethics sections, the references (skimmed for origins), and Appendix A.1–A.7 and B.1–B.2, including Tables 6–22. Nothing was skipped.

CLAIMS
- claim: In the supervised setting, a FiD-xl (3B) reader that reads 10 documents generated by InstructGPT, with no retrieval at all, beats the published DPR-FiD on TriviaQA and WebQ. It loses on NQ.
  number: TQA 71.6, WebQ 54.4, NQ 45.6 EM. Published FiD (770M, 100 Wikipedia docs) scores 67.6 / 50.5 / 51.4. The paper's own FiD-xl (DPR, 10 docs) scores 66.3 / 50.8 / 50.1.
  setup: Open-test splits. Generator is text-davinci-002 (175B). Clustering prompts. The FiD reader is fine-tuned on each dataset's training split. The abstract's "+4.0 and +3.9" is measured against the published FiD-770M with 100 docs (71.6−67.6, 54.4−50.5), not against the authors' own 10-doc FiD-xl.
  quote: "GENREAD (FiD-xl) (clustering) 3B 10 71.6 54.4 45.6 57.1" / "FiD (Izacard & Grave, 2021) 770M 100 67.6 50.5 51.4 56.5" / "outperforming the state-of-the-artretrieve-then-read pipeline DPR-FiD by +4.0 and +3.9, without retrieving any documents"
  where: Table 2, p8; abstract, p1
- claim: Merging retrieved and generated documents beats either source alone. This is the paper's best result.
  number: averages 61.5 EM merged vs 57.1 generated-only vs 55.7 DPR. The gains are +5.7 over DPR and +4.4 over the LLM.
  setup: Supervised, FiD-xl, TQA / WebQ / NQ. The merged row reads "74.3 56.2 54.0 61.5".
  quote: "merge retrieved documents with generated documents 74.3 56.2 54.0 61.5" / "it can improve +5.7 averagely on three open-domain QA benchmarks compared to DPR alone, and improve +4.4 averagely compared to the large language model alone."
  where: Table 2, p8; §4.3.1, p9
- claim: Swapping 10 of the K DPR documents for 10 LLM-generated documents beats DPR alone at the same total K, from K=20 to K=100.
  number: none in text (shown as a curve)
  setup: FiD-l reader, because FiD-xl runs out of memory on A100s above 20 docs. Total document count is held fixed.
  quote: "we replace 10 documents retrieved by DPR with 10 documents generated by LLM so the total number of documents is the same."
  where: Figure 3 caption, p9
- claim: In the zero-shot setting, writing a background document first and then answering beats asking InstructGPT directly. Generator and reader are the same model.
  number: GenRead 28.0 / 59.0 / 24.6 vs no-docs 20.9 / 57.5 / 18.6 (NQ / TQA / WebQ EM)
  setup: InstructGPT 175B, greedy decoding. The numbers are averaged over 3 reading prompts (Table 20). The text claims "+6.9", but I cannot reproduce that from the v3 tables (see PROBLEMS).
  quote: "InstructGPT (no docs.) 20.9 57.5 18.6" / "GENREAD (InstructGPT) 28.0 59.0 24.6" / "GENREAD can improve the EM score by +6.9 on three open-domain QA benchmarks, compared to the original InstructGPT."
  where: Table 1, p6; §4.1.1, p6
- claim: In the zero-shot setting, GenRead roughly matches retrieve-then-read with the same reader. It beats BM25 and Contriever on all three QA sets, and Google search on TQA and WebQ. On NQ it trails DPR and Google.
  number: NQ: DPR+InstructGPT 29.1, Google 28.8, GenRead 28.0. WebQ: 20.2 / 20.4 / 24.6.
  setup: Each pipeline puts one document into the prompt read by InstructGPT. DPR is supervised on these datasets.
  quote: "DPR + InstructGPT* 29.1 53.8 20.2" / "Google + InstructGPT 28.8 58.8 20.4" / "GENREAD can achieve on-par performance with zero-shot retrieve-then-read pipeline models on the NQ and FM2 datasets, and outperform them on all other benchmarks."
  where: Table 1 and §4.1.1, p6
- claim: Generated documents contain the answer more often than retrieved ones at small K. The advantage shrinks as K grows, and on NQ DPR wins.
  number: R@1 on TQA is 69.6 (clustering) vs 53.2 (DPR). R@20 on NQ is 74.5 vs 79.5.
  setup: Test sets. R@K is the percentage of the top-K documents that contain the answer.
  quote: "DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020) 53.2 75.3 79.0 45.4 70.5 75.2 44.6 74.5 79.5" / "GENREAD (clustering prompts) 69.6 82.9 85.1 54.5 73.3 75.4 48.0 70.9 74.5" / "the slope of the curve decreases as the number of generated documents increases"
  where: Table 10, p17; §4.2.2, p7
- claim: Clustering prompts improve over plain nucleus sampling, because repeated sampling from one prompt produces near-duplicate documents.
  number: +2.2 EM on average. Table 2 averages are 57.1 vs 54.9 (FiD-xl).
  setup: K-means over GPT-3 embeddings (12,288-dim) of question-document pairs from the training set. n=5 demonstrations are drawn from each cluster. Nucleus sampling uses p=.95.
  quote: "the clustering-based prompt method can improve the EM score by +2.2 on average"
  where: §4.2.2, p8
- claim: In the ablation, sampling the demonstrations from within a cluster beats sampling them from the whole dataset.
  number: TQA EM 71.8 vs 70.9
  setup: Table 11, five demonstrations
  quote: "Sample 5 documents from each cluster 82.7 71.8 73.3 54.4 70.6 45.3"
  where: Table 11, p17
- claim: Generating context only beats retrieval with the largest model. Smaller InstructGPT generators fall below DPR-FiD.
  number: Davinci-175B reaches 69.6 TQA vs DPR-FiD 66.3. The smaller generators score far lower (e.g. 52.6 / 44.6 / 37.4 on TQA as plotted).
  setup: Ada-150M, Babbage-1.3B, Curie-6.7B and Davinci-175B generators, with a FiD-xl reader and 10 docs.
  quote: "Only with the largest size InstructGPT, GENREAD can outperform the DPR-FiD."
  where: §A.4, Figure 4, p16
- claim: With an open model as generator, results are weaker but comparable to DPR.
  number: OPT 62.1 / 51.8 vs DPR 66.3 / 50.8 (TQA / WebQ). Codex scores 72.6 / 55.4.
  setup: Same FiD pipeline as Table 2. The text calls Codex "open-source", which is incorrect.
  quote: "OPT (Zhang et al., 2022) 62.1 51.8"
  where: Table 8, p16
- claim: The NQ deficit is attributed to time-dependent questions and incomplete labels.
  number: About 16.5% of NQ questions are time-dependent. In 100 audited examples, 29 have annotation problems (13 temporal, 16 incomplete), and 8% are hallucinations.
  setup: Manual case study of 100 GenRead NQ predictions.
  quote: "NQ contains a signiﬁcant proportion, roughly 16.5%, of questions that have time-dependent answers" / "we found that 29 examples have data collection and annotation mistakes, mainly including the temporal question issue (13 / 29) and the incomplete answer issue (16 / 29)"
  where: §A.7, p18; Table 12, p19
- claim: When both documents contain the answer, FiD reads the generated one more accurately.
  number: TQA 86.8 vs 80.2
  setup: Subset where both the DPR document and the generated document contain the answer.
  quote: "GENREAD (clustering prompts) 64.0 86.8 66.7"
  where: Table 5, p9
- claim: GenRead only matches dense retrieval on fact checking.
  number: FEVER 89.6 vs FiD 90.2. Merging both sources gives 91.8.
  setup: Supervised, KILT splits
  quote: "GENREAD (FiD-xl) (clustering) 89.6 77.8 19.1 / 16.8"
  where: Table 3, p8
- claim: In FLOPs, generation costs less than DPR only below about 2,473 questions, because DPR's one-time encoding of 21M Wikipedia passages amortises over the queries.
  number: break-even at X≈2473
  setup: Kaplan FLOPs-per-token estimate. The authors note that FLOPs are not real cost.
  quote: "if the number of input questions is less than 2473, the total cost of InstructGPT is lower than the DPR"
  where: §A.6, p18

LIMITS
- The authors concede that knowledge cannot be updated without retraining: "our approach is limited in its ability to update knowledge state and adapt to new domains... adding new knowledge would likely require some retraining." (p10)
- They concede hallucination: "generated documents might suffer from hallucination error, resulting in incorrect predictions" (p10). Table 15 shows the cases, e.g. generated "Virginia Declaration of Rights" (George Mason) for "first declaration of human rights".
- The ethics section on p10 adds that generated documents "suffer from challenges of stale information from outdated documents used for training", are "less diverse, potentially biasing answers towards more common entities", and that experiments ran on "only three large language models".
- What the paper does not show:
  - It never measures freshness or hallucination rates systematically. It gives case studies only, plus 8/100 NQ.
  - There is no private or domain corpus. Everything is Wikipedia-trivia benchmarks that the LLM very likely saw in training, so the closed-book advantage is a best case.
  - Generated documents carry no attribution or citation.
  - Results depend on one generator (text-davinci-002, now deprecated) and need a ≥175B model.
  - Most comparisons use 10 documents, not FiD's standard 100.
  - Results are EM only, with no human evaluation of answer correctness beyond case studies.
- What has dated: the baselines (DPR, FiD, GPT-3-era models) are 2020–2022.

BUILDS ON
- Retrieve-then-read: Karpukhin et al., 2020 (DPR); Izacard & Grave, 2021 (FiD); Lewis et al., 2020 (RAG); Lee et al., 2019 (ORQA); Chen et al., 2017 (BM25 reader).
- LMs as knowledge stores: Petroni et al., 2019; Roberts et al., 2020; Levine et al., 2022.
- Generated knowledge: Liu et al. (2022b), generated knowledge prompting; Mao et al., 2021 (generation-augmented retrieval).
- Generator: Ouyang et al., 2022 (InstructGPT). Prompts come from Bach et al., 2022 (P3/PromptSource). Nucleus sampling is Holtzman et al., 2020.
- Temporality: Zhang & Choi, 2021 (SituatedQA).

CODE (prompts, verbatim)
- Generate step, zero-shot QA (p26, §B.1.2): "Generate a background document from Wikipedia to answer the given question.\n\n{query}\ n\n"
- Read step (p26, §B.1.3, prompt 1): "Refer to the passage below and answer the following question with just a few words. Passage: {background}\ n\n Question:{query}\ n\n The answer is"
- Closed-book baseline (p26): "{query}\ n\n The answer is"

FIGURES
- Figure 3, p9: "Combining DPR retrieved documents and large language model (LLM) generated documents can achieve significantly better performance than using DPR retrieved documents only." This is the best candidate for "the knowledge gap". It shows in one glance that parametric and retrieved knowledge are complementary, and that the answer is "both", not "pick one". It is a three-panel EM-vs-K plot for NQ, TQA and WebQ.
- Alternatives:
  - Figure 2, p7: Recall@K for generated vs DPR vs Google. It shows that generation wins at small K and loses its edge as K grows.
  - Figure 1, p4: the clustering-prompt pipeline.
  - Figure 4, p16: the generator-size scaling curve. Generation only beats retrieval at 175B.

PROBLEMS
- Headline numbers do not add up:
  - I cannot reproduce the zero-shot "+6.9" from the v3 tables. Table 1 gives average gains of about +4.9 (7.1 / 1.5 / 6.0), and Table 9's open-test columns give about +5.2. Table 1 carries "Note: fix numbers in v2", so the +6.9 is probably a stale v1 figure. Cite the table values instead.
  - §A.7 says "Among the 22 incorrect predictions, 12 ... retrieval errors ... and 12 as reading errors". That sums to 24, and Table 12 shows wrong retrieval 12% and wrong reading 10%.
- Prose that contradicts its own tables or cites the wrong table:
  - §4.3.2 says generated text "tends to have lower coverage than retrieved documents", but Table 4 shows GenRead coverage higher than DPR on TriviaQA and WebQ (76.5 vs 67.3, 62.1 vs 58.8) and lower only on NQ (61.7 vs 67.9).
  - The text points to "Table 6" for the Recall@K and coverage numbers. Table 6 is dataset statistics; the numbers are in Table 10.
- Extraction faults: some words run together (e.g. "state-of-the-artretrieve-then-read"), and the figure axes come out as stray numbers. Table contents extracted legibly.
- The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
